description: Per-repo literature sub-index for cslib metalogic work. Temporal/Bimodal (tasks 180, 444-446, 464) and Constructive Modal CK-cube (tasks 501, 508, 509). Reference-only doc_id pointers into the global Literature/ repo.

entries.relevance: Burgess 'Axioms for tense logic I: Since and Until' — primary source for the Since/Until axiomatization (Burgess1982I citations in task 446).
Burgess 'Axioms for tense logic II: Time periods' — Burgess1982II disambiguation for task 446 citation hygiene.
Reynolds — the Burgess-Xu completeness result and IRR rule; directly relevant to base-BX completeness w.r.t. serial/ordered domains (task 445 obstruction).
Venema on Since/Until conservativity and completeness over classes of linear orders (task 445 conservativity).
Venema anti-axioms / conservativity questions for temporal logics.
Gabbay — irreflexivity rule and axiomatization of U,S over general linear time; completeness machinery for the domain-transfer question (task 445).
Goldblatt, Logics of Time and Computation — completeness of temporal logics over ordered domains; frame classes and correspondence.
Rabinovich, 'A Proof of Kamp's Theorem' — expressive-completeness of Since/Until over the reals; central reference for structure-first MPL expressiveness arguments (task 464).
Caleiro, Viganò, Volpe — mosaic method for many-dimensional modal logics; structural completeness technique supporting the structure-first design argument (task 464).
Hodkinson & Reynolds, 'Temporal Logic' (Handbook of Modal Logic, Ch. 11) — comprehensive survey of temporal-logic expressiveness and axiomatization (task 464).

Blackburn, de Rijke, Venema, Modal Logic (2002 Cambridge ed.) — model-theoretic and structural methods for the structure-first MPL argument (task 464); also Loewenheim-Skolem, bounded morphisms, and model-theoretic transfer methods relevant to the countermodel-transport strategy (task 445).

Wijesekera, Constructive Modal Logics I (APAL 1990): canonical source for independent, non-interdefinable box/diamond in constructive modal logic; backs the modal Basic.lean primitive-design rationale and replaces the misattributed Blackburn2001 citation (task 499).

Chagrov & Zakharyaschev, Modal Logic (Oxford Logic Guides 35, 1997): reference for intermediate/superintuitionistic logics; now locally backed, so the ChagrovZakharyaschev1997 citation in references.bib is no longer an orphan (task 499).
Bierman & de Paiva, On an Intuitionistic Modal Logic (Studia Logica 2000): constructive modal logic CK with both modalities primitive; supporting citation for independent box/diamond (task 499).

Simpson, Proof Theory and Semantics of Intuitionistic Modal Logic (PhD thesis, Edinburgh 1994): the canonical reference for independent, non-interdefinable box/diamond; primary replacement citation for the modal Basic.lean primitive-design rationale (task 499).

Pacheco, Collapsing Constructive and Intuitionistic Modal Logics (arXiv:2408.16428, 2024) — PRIMARY SOURCE for task 509. Works in the CK fallible-world / primitive-diamond setting with CKB := CK + {B_box, B_dia}, exactly the cslib bBox/bDia axioms. Theorem 13: CKB proves phi iff IKB proves phi iff CKB validates phi. Canonical model built over prime, CONSISTENT, NON-MAXIMAL theories. Lemma 15 derives symmetry directly from B_dia (dia box P implies P) by using the DIAMOND-inverse relation (Gamma ~ Delta iff Gamma subset Delta and Delta subset Gamma-dia), sidestepping the maximality obstruction that blocks the box-inverse definition. Canonical W_bot is empty, which explains task 508 cs5_dia_bot_imp_bot and the Set.univ-free tail lead.

Arisaka, Das, Strassburger, On Nested Sequents for Constructive Modal Logics (LMCS 11(3:7), 2015) — deepest proof-theoretic treatment of the fallible-world constructive modal cube including CS5. Section 4.3 proves B entails k3 (diamond distribution) and k5 (not dia bot) constructively, corroborating the collapse result. Explicitly disclaims Kripke-semantic completeness for CS5, supporting the scope caveat in task 509.

Alechina, Mendler, de Paiva, Ritter, Categorical and Kripke Semantics for Constructive S4 (CSL 2001, LNCS 2142:292-307) — INGESTED task 512. The constructive (Wijesekera) diamond birelational completeness. Saturation Lemma 1 builds worlds as consistent-theory PAIRS (Gamma, Delta) with Delta a prime filter (NO negation-completeness). Section 5 proves the constructive diamond REQUIRES fallible worlds + refutation-sets Delta (pair worlds), redundant only if dia-bot and dia-distribution are adopted. Establishes that CSLib's constructive-diamond CS5 needs pair/fallible canonical worlds (= its own CKSegment head+tail), NOT Dosen's single-prime-theory model. S4 only (no symmetry).

Marin, Morales, Strassburger, A Fully Labelled Proof System for Intuitionistic Modal Logics (J. Logic Comput. 31(3):998-1022, 2021) — INGESTED task 512. Whole intuitionistic modal cube IK-IS5 with birelational semantics. Def 2.1: F1/F2 confluence conditions. Theorem 7.1 [Plotkin-Stirling 1986]: symmetry (b) and Euclidean (5) are Scott-Lemmon path axioms whose frame condition is a ONE-SIDED, <=-mediated intuitionistic klmn-incestuality condition (NOT naive classical symmetry). Theorem 7.2: soundness + completeness for the whole family incl IS5, no negation-completeness (saturated/prime sets). Remark 7.3: naive frame conditions are 'problematic' -- diagnoses CSLib's two-sided-tail as the wrong (negation-completeness-requiring) symmetry condition.

Massacci, Single Step Tableaux for Modal Logics (JAR 24(3):319-364, 2000). Terminating single-step/prefixed tableau calculi uniformly across the modal cube incl. S5/K5/KB5; loop-checking & prefix-management termination where the edge-local modal-depth-decrement measure fails. Primary source for task 514/515 (unblocking task 504 S5 termination obstruction, modalApplyOneS5_rankStep_not_dischargeable). BibKey Massacci2000.

Verified completeness in Henkin-style for intuitionistic propositional logic — First verified Henkin-style completeness proof for intuitionistic propositional logic following Troelstra and van Dalen's method, implemented in Lean with prime extension lemma.
Introduction to Mathematical Logic — Front Matter — migrated from the repository-local literature directory
SeCaV: A Sequent Calculus Verifier in Isabelle/HOL — Formalizes soundness and completeness for sequent calculus in Isabelle/HOL, relevant as comparative prior art for CSLib's proof system.

Temporal Logic: Mathematical Foundations — Chapter 10: Temporal Logic over the Integers — Chapter 10 of GHR94: Separation Theorem for temporal logic over integers (Theorem 10.2.9) and completeness proof for the Until-Since tense logic over ℤ; basis for CSLib's bimodal separation proof.
Investigations into Logical Deduction — Synopsis and Notation — Synopsis and notation for Gentzen's foundational paper introducing natural deduction (NJ, NK) and sequent calculus (LJ, LK).

The Completeness of the First-Order Functional Calculus — Original Henkin completeness proof for first-order logic using maximal consistent set extension, the method adapted in CSLib for propositional and modal completeness proofs.
A New Introduction to Modal Logic — Preface and Contents — Preface and TOC for Hughes & Cresswell's introduction to modal logic.

Der Minimalkalkül, ein reduzierter intuitionistischer Formalismus — Defines minimal logic by removing ex falso quodlibet from Heyting's intuitionistic system, retaining falsum as a primitive and negation defined as A→⊥.
Introduction to Mathematical Logic (6th ed.) — Front Matter — Front matter for Mendelson's standard mathematical logic textbook (6th edition).
Structural Proof Theory — Front matter: preface, table of contents, overview

Introduction to a General Theory of Elementary Propositions — Proved functional completeness of propositional connectives and introduced truth tables systematically; foundational for CSLib's Evaluate/Tautology definitions.
Basic Proof Theory — Front matter: preface, table of contents, notation

Intuitionistic Propositional Logic in Lean — Formalizes strong completeness for intuitionistic propositional logic in Lean with both Kripke and algebraic semantics, directly comparable to CSLib's approach.

Advanced Modal Logic — Introduction — Introduction to the Advanced Modal Logic handbook chapter, providing historical overview and roadmap for unimodal, polymodal, and superintuitionistic logic sections.
